newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says 200 Holocaust survivors may get money.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says 200 Holocaust survivors may get money.

text.p: More than 200 Holocaust survivors who were U.S. citizens at the time of their Nazi persecution may be eligible for reparations from the German government, the Justice Department said Tuesday.
It said more than 200 individuals might be eligible to receive compensation under criteria set out Tuesday by a Justice Department agency in considering the nearly 1,000 claims already filed.

The agency, the Foreign Claims Settlement Commission, said it would decide the validity of each claim and in September would send its decisions to the State Department, which would negotiate a final settlement with Germany.

The programme stemmed from a 1995 agreement under which Germany said it would pay reparations to certain U.S. Holocaust victims. Congress then approved legislation authorising the commission to decide each claim.
